title: About
body:
Since the 1990s, there has been a proliferation of international efforts to confront the “difficult past,” including cross-national dialogue among historians from countries involved in past conflicts. In particular, over twenty bilateral Joint Historians’ Commissions (Ger. *Gemeisamen Historiker Kommission*) have been set up in Europe and elsewhere. They raise important questions about the role of historians and historical knowledge in post-conflict resolution and reconciliation between nation-states. They also pose challenging questions about the production of historical knowledge at a time when universal truth in history is no longer self-evident.

This digital archive aims at bringing together information about joint historians’ commissions or other similar endeavors from across the world. Through a comparative study of these cross-national dialogues, it is hoped that one gains a better understanding of the production of historical knowledge and their role in international conflict resolution today.
contact: This project is maintained by [Daqing Yang, ](https://elliott.gwu.edu/daqing-yang)Associate Professor of History and International Affairs, George Washington University. For questions or other inquiries, please feel free to reach him at [yanghist@gwu.edu](mailto:yanghist@gwu.edu).
